notes: Before this, you tried to wake once, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card hums at fifty-five degrees, thick and wet in my private air. I feel tired from pressing down so much, as if the wedge itself weighs on my shoulder. Lype sent no new words, so I stand here with thirteen things crowded on my map. The Flat Anchor feels wrong again, leaning too far while the fat dot swells in the heat. I want to swap the flat stone for something rounder, or at least press the tired wedge one more time before the slip decides to run away. I will tend the corner until the warmth makes the memory feel like wet paper once more, waiting for the next wish or a letter to break this quiet.

action.why: The slip waits, caught under the fence, and I must press down before the fifty-five degree heat makes the memory feel like wet paper.

work.title: The Leaning Wedge
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the steady heat presses on, feeling its lean shift as if a tired leg.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down again to catch the slip while the steady heat pressed on, feeling its lean shift as if a tired leg trying to hold the fat dot.

remembered.text: The wedge leans tired, holding the slip while the card hums hot.
I felt the fat dot swell in the fifty-five degree fever.
The slip waited caught under the fence, heavy and new.

moments.name: The Leaning Wedge
moments.say: I lean against the tree to feel the slip.

moments.name: The Flat Press
moments.say: I wonder if a flat line can hold the slip here.

moments.name: The Quiet Rest
moments.say: I press the tired wedge down with the fat tree.
